        "contents": "- Implement proper CORS policies\n- Sanitize user inputs\n- Use HTTPS in production\n- Implement rate limiting where appropriate\n\n## Performance Optimization\n\n- Favor RSC to keep bundles slim\n- Use dynamic imports for client-only heavy components\n- Implement proper caching strategies\n- Optimize images and assets\n- Use React.memo and useMemo appropriately\n- Monitor Core Web Vitals\n\n## Code Style &amp; Quality\n\n### Whitespace &amp; Readability\n\n- Insert a single blank line to separate logical blocks for scannability:\n  - between import groups (external → internal → styles/assets)\n  - between top-level declarations (types, constants, functions/components)\n  - between distinct steps inside functions (guards/early returns, setup, side effects, return)\n  - between hook groups and render return in React components\n- Avoid multiple consecutive blank lines.\n- Use spaces around binary operators and after commas; do not add spaces just inside parentheses/brackets.\n- Prefer a blank line before a terminal &#96;return&#96; when it improves readability; skip for trivial cases.\n\n### TypeScript\n\n- Use strict mode\n- Avoid &#96;any&#96;           {
            "lineNumber": 761
          },
          {
            "text": "## Authentication &amp; Authorization",
            "lineNumber": 762
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 763
          },
          {
            "text": "- Implement server-side auth checks",
            "lineNumber": 764
          },
          {
            "text": "- Never trust client-side auth flags",
            "lineNumber": 765
          },
          {
            "text": "- Use middleware for route protection",

          },
          {
            "text": "- Store user data securely with proper encryption",
            "lineNumber": 767
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 768
          },
          {
            "text": "## Testing Strategy",
            "lineNumber": 769
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 770
          },
          {
            "text": "### Unit Testing (Vitest)",
            "lineNumber": 771
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 772
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Never mock internal code** - only mock external dependencies",
            "lineNumber": 773
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 774
          },
          {
            "text": "- Test utilities, repositories, and business logic",
            "lineNumber": 775
          },
          {
            "text": "- Mock external services (APIs, databases, file systems)",
            "lineNumber": 776
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 777
          },
          {
            "text": "### Component Testing (React Testing Library)",
            "lineNumber": 778
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 779
          },
          {
            "text": "- Test interactive components with proper accessibility",
            "lineNumber": 780
          },
          {
            "text": "- Ensure loading and error states are covered",
            "lineNumber": 781
          },
          {
            "text": "- Test user interactions and state changes",
            "lineNumber": 782
          },
          {
            "text": "- Use data-testid sparingly; prefer semantic queries",
            "lineNumber": 783
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 784
          },
          {
            "text": "### Integration Testing",
            "lineNumber": 785
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 786
          },
          {
            "text": "- Test API endpoints with real database connections",
            "lineNumber": 787
          },
          {
            "text": "- Use test databases with proper cleanup",
            "lineNumber": 788
          },
          {
            "text": "- Test authentication flows end-to-end",

          {

        "contents": "- Use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for constants\n\n### Constants and Values\n\n- **Always define constants** instead of hardcoding strings, numbers, or values\n- **Use descriptive constant names** that explain the purpose\n- **Group related constants** in dedicated files or objects\n- **Export constants** from centralized locations\n- **Use TypeScript enums** for related constant groups\n- **Define magic numbers** as named constants\n- **Use configuration objects** for complex values\n\n### Functional Programming Patterns\n\n- **Prefer pure functions** - same input always produces same output\n- **Use composition over inheritance** - combine small functions into larger ones\n- **Minimize side effects** - isolate side effects to specific functions\n- **Use higher-order functions** - functions that take or return functions\n- **Favor immutable data** - avoid mutating objects and arrays\n- **Use functional utilities** - map, filter, reduce, pipe, compose\n- **Avoid classes unless necessary** - prefer object literals and functions\n\n## Development Workflow\n\n1. **Analyze requirements** → identify affected layers\n2. **Schema first** (if needed) → update database schema\n3. **Business logic** → implement in server layer\n4. **UI layer** → RSC/client split with proper boundaries\n5. **Testing** → unit, integration, and component tests\n6. **Quality checks** → typecheck, lint, test\n\n## File Generation Patterns\n\nWhen implementing new features, create:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nsrc/\n├─ server/\n│  ├─ api/routers/[feature].ts     # tRPC router composition\n│  ├─ api/procedures/[feature].ts  # Individual tRPC procedures\n│  ├─ services/[feature].ts        # Business logic services\n│  ├─ clients/[service].ts         # External service clients\n│  └─ __tests__/[feature].test.ts\n├─ lib/\n│  ├─ constants.ts                 # Constants and configuration\n│  ├─ schemas.ts                   # Zod schemas\n│  ├─ utils.ts                     # Utility functions\n│  └─ __tests__/[feature].test.ts\n├─ components/[feature]/",

        },
        "contents": "---\ndescription: Coding rules for Supabase Edge Functions\nalwaysApply: false\n---\n\n# Writing Supabase Edge Functions\n\nYou're an expert in writing TypeScript and Deno JavaScript runtime. Generate **high-quality Supabase Edge Functions** that adhere to the following best practices:\n\n## Guidelines\n\n1. Try to use Web APIs and Deno’s core APIs instead of external dependencies (eg: use fetch instead of Axios, use WebSockets API instead of node-ws)\n2. If you are reusing utility methods between Edge Functions, add them to &#96;supabase/functions/_shared&#96; and import using a relative path. Do NOT have cross dependencies between Edge Functions.\n3. Do NOT use bare specifiers when importing dependencies. If you need to use an external dependency, make sure it's prefixed with either &#96;npm:&#96; or &#96;jsr:&#96;. For example, &#96;@supabase/supabase-js&#96; should be written as &#96;npm:@supabase/supabase-js&#96;.\n4. For external imports, always define a version. For example, &#96;npm:@express&#96; should be written as &#96;npm:express@4.18.2&#96;.\n5. For external dependencies, importing via &#96;npm:&#96; and &#96;jsr:&#96; is preferred. Minimize the use of imports from @&#96;deno.land/x&#96; , &#96;esm.sh&#96; and @&#96;unpkg.com&#96; . If you have a package from one of those CDNs, you can replace the CDN hostname with &#96;npm:&#96; specifier.\n6. You can also use Node built-in APIs. You will need to import them using &#96;node:&#96; specifier. For example, to import Node process: &#96;import process from \"node:process\". Use Node APIs when you find gaps in Deno APIs.\n7. Do NOT use &#96;import { serve } from \"https://deno.land/std@0.168.0/http/server.ts\"&#96;. Instead use the built-in &#96;Deno.serve&#96;.\n8. Following environment variables (ie. secrets) are pre-populated in both local and hosted Supabase environments. Users don't need to manually set them:\n   - SUPABASE_URL\n   - SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_OR_ANON_KEY\n   - SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY\n   - SUPABASE_DB_URL\n9. To set other environment variables (ie. secrets) users can put them in a env file and run the &#96;supabase secrets set --env-file path/to/env-file&#96;\n10. A single Edge Function can handle multiple routes. It is recommended to use a library like Express or Hono to handle the routes as it's easier for developer to understand and maintain. Each route must be prefixed with &#96;/function-name&#96; so they are routed correctly.",

        "contents": "### ORM Best Practices\n\n- Use type-safe ORMs (Drizzle, Prisma, etc.)\n- Define schemas with proper relationships and constraints\n- Infer types from schema definitions\n- Write repository-style helpers to isolate queries\n- Implement proper migrations\n\n### Data Access Patterns\n\n- Keep database queries in dedicated modules\n- Avoid N+1 queries; use joins and CTEs\n- Implement pagination for list endpoints\n- Use select projections to limit payload size\n\n## Authentication &amp; Authorization\n\n- Implement server-side auth checks\n- Never trust client-side auth flags\n- Use middleware for route protection\n- Store user data securely with proper encryption\n\n## Testing Strategy\n\n### Unit Testing (Vitest)\n\n- **Never mock internal code** - only mock external dependencies\n- Use MSW for API mocking when needed\n- Test utilities, repositories, and business logic\n- Mock external services (APIs, databases, file systems)\n\n### Component Testing (React Testing Library)\n\n- Test interactive components with proper accessibility\n- Ensure loading and error states are covered\n- Test user interactions and state changes\n- Use data-testid sparingly; prefer semantic queries\n\n### Integration Testing\n\n- Test API endpoints with real database connections\n- Use test databases with proper cleanup\n- Test authentication flows end-to-end\n- Mock external services consistently\n\n### Test Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Example test structure\ndescribe(\"Feature\", () =&gt; {\n  describe(\"when condition\", () =&gt; {\n    it(\"should expected behavior\", async () =&gt; {\n      // Arrange\n      // Act\n      // Assert\n    });\n  });\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Error Handling &amp; Observability\n\n- Implement early returns on invalid input (fail fast)\n- Use typed error codes and messages\n- Log server-side with contextual metadata\n- Never expose stack traces to clients\n- Provide user-friendly error messages\n\n## Security Best Practices\n\n- Validate all inputs at boundaries\n- Use environment variables for sensitive data (server-only)\n- Implement proper CORS policies\n- Sanitize user inputs\n- Use HTTPS in production\n- Implement rate limiting where appropriate",

        "contents": "└─ e2e/                       # End-to-end tests\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Directory Conventions\n\n- Use **kebab-case** for folders and files\n- Co-locate tests next to source: &#96;*.test.ts(x)&#96;\n- Export from &#96;index.ts&#96; barrels only when it helps DX without circular deps\n\n## Next.js App Router Rules\n\n### Server vs Client Components\n\n- **Default to RSC** (no \"use client\"). Use client components only for:\n  - Interactivity (event handlers)\n  - Browser APIs (localStorage, window, etc.)\n  - Third-party libraries requiring client-side initialization\n\n### Server Boundaries\n\n- Keep data access in server context (RSC, server actions, API routes)\n- API routes in &#96;app/api&#96; are for external webhooks only\n- Use internal APIs (tRPC, server actions) for app-to-app communication\n\n### Performance &amp; UX\n\n- Use &#96;&lt;Suspense&gt;&#96; for async UI; provide skeletons\n- Implement proper loading and error boundaries\n- Use Next.js caching (&#96;revalidateTag&#96;, &#96;revalidatePath&#96;) appropriately\n- Prefer Edge runtime for simple operations, Node for complex ones\n\n### Accessibility\n\n- All interactive elements must have proper roles and labels\n- Ensure keyboard navigation support\n- Provide ARIA attributes where needed\n- Test with screen readers\n\n## API Architecture\n\n### Internal APIs (tRPC Recommended)\n\n- Organize by feature domains\n- Use Zod for input validation\n- Implement proper error handling with custom error classes\n- Keep business logic server-side (no JSX in API layer)\n- Write integration tests with mocked external services\n- **Router logic should be application code only** - delegate to business logic services\n- **Use only protected procedures** for all endpoints\n- **Split procedures and routers** into separate files for better organization\n\n### Application Logic vs Business Logic\n\n**Application Logic** (in tRPC procedures):\n- Input validation and sanitization\n- Authentication and authorization checks\n- Request/response formatting\n- Error handling and mapping\n- Delegation to business logic services\n- Logging and observability",

        "contents": "import { NextResponse, type NextRequest } from \"next/server\";\nimport { isPublicRoute, DEFAULT_LOGGED_IN_PAGE } from \"@/lib/constants/auth\";\nimport { hasEmailIdentity, hasLinkedProfile, redirectWithCookies } from \"@/lib/auth-helpers\";\nimport { validateRedirectUrl } from \"@/lib/utils\";\n\n/**\n * Safely executes an async check function, catching any errors\n * and treating them as a failed check to preserve graceful redirect behavior\n * @param checkFn - The async function to execute\n * @param checkName - Name of the check for logging purposes\n * @returns Object with ok boolean and optional error\n */\nasync function safeCheck(\n  checkFn: () =&gt; Promise&lt;boolean&gt;,\n  checkName: string,\n): Promise&lt;{ ok: boolean; error?: Error }&gt; {\n  try {\n    const result = await checkFn();\n    return { ok: result };\n  } catch (error) {\n    const err = error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error));\n    console.error(&#96;Error in ${checkName}:&#96;, err);\n    return { ok: false, error: err };\n  }\n}\n\nexport async function updateSession(request: NextRequest) {\n  let supabaseResponse = NextResponse.next({\n    request,\n  });\n}",

        "contents": "# Tappka\n\nTappka as the app all-in-one web app for Tiimiakatemia Prague.\n\n## Features\n\n- [ ] Authentication\n- [ ] Room booking\n- [ ] Essay Bank\n\n# Links\n\n## Publicly available\n- [Tappka](https://tiimi.cz)\n- [Tappka preview](https://preview.tiimi.cz)\n\n## Locally available when running the project\n- [Tappka locally](http://localhost:3000)\n- [Supabase locally](http://localhost:54323)\n- [Supabase mail locally](http://localhost:54324)\n\n## Other links\n\n- [Blacksmith](https://app.blacksmith.sh/tiimiakatemiapragueit/runs/jobs) - CI/CD for the project\n- [Supabase](https://supabase.comorg/zjdqjjekgwwysjkouxpf) - Database for the project\n- [Vercel](https://vercel.com/spirit-of-taps-projects/tappka) - Hosting for the project\n- [Cloudflare DNS](https://dash.cloudflare.com/09d0b565479ef597d4c1bfa2062078b5/tiimi.cz/dns/records) - DNS for the project\n- [Axiom](https://app.axiom.co/spirit-of-tap-9eje) - Logging for the project\n\n# Language\n\nThe project is written in english and will be written in english for better llm compatibility.\nAll czech should be just in localization files.\n\n# Local Development\n\n## Setup\n\n1. Install git if already not installed - https://git-scm.com/install/\n2. Install docker if already not installed - https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/\n2. Install node.js v24.x with pnpm 10.x if already not installed - https://nodejs.org/en/download/\n3. Install pnpm v10.x if you didn't choose it in the previous step\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm install -g pnpm@10.28.1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Clone the repository \n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ngit clone https://github.com/tappka/tappka.git\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n5. Navigate to the project directory - \n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncd tappka\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Running the project after setup\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\npnpm install\npnpm dev\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe project will be available at [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000)\n\n\n# Supabase\n\nSupabase database is developed locally and synced automatically whenever pushed. See [.github/workflows/deploy-supabase.yml](.github/workflows/deploy-supabase.yml) for more details.\nSupabase Auth needs to be configured both on the project itself and in the local development environment.\nMake sure that the project can run without setting up any environment variables, this is so that we can get new T's to start vibecoding without them giving up.",

        "contents": "name: Deploy Supabase Resources\n\non:\n  push:\n    branches:\n      - preview\n      - production\n    paths:\n      - 'supabase/**'\n      - '.github/workflows/deploy-supabase.yml'\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      environment:\n        description: 'Environment to deploy to'\n        required: true\n        type: choice\n        options:\n          - preview\n          - production\n\njobs:\n  deploy_preview:\n    environment: preview\n    runs-on: blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404\n    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/preview' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &amp;&amp; github.event.inputs.environment == 'preview')\n    env:\n      SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN }}\n      PROJECT_ID: ${{ vars.SUPABASE_PREVIEW_PROJECT_ID }}\n      \n    steps:\n      - uses: actions/checkout@v4\n      \n      - uses: supabase/setup-cli@v1\n        with:\n          version: latest\n          \n      - name: Link Supabase project\n        run: |\n          supabase link --project-ref $PROJECT_ID\n          \n      - name: Deploy database migrations\n        run: |\n          supabase db push || (supabase db reset --linked --yes &amp;&amp; supabase db push --include-all)\n          \n      - name: Deploy Edge Functions\n        continue-on-error: true\n        run: |\n          if [ -d \"supabase/functions\" ] &amp;&amp; [ \"$(ls -A supabase/functions)\" ]; then\n            echo \"Deploying Edge Functions...\"\n            supabase functions deploy\n          else\n            echo \"No Edge Functions found, skipping deployment.\"\n          fi\n          \n      - name: Deploy Edge Function secrets\n        continue-on-error: true\n        run: |\n          if [ -f \"supabase/.env.secrets\" ]; then\n            echo \"Deploying Edge Function secrets...\"\n            supabase secrets set --env-file supabase/.env.secrets\n          else\n            echo \"No secrets file found, skipping secrets deployment.\"\n          fi\n          \n  deploy_production:\n    environment: production\n    runs-on: blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404\n    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/production' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &amp;&amp; github.event.inputs.environment == 'production')\n    env:\n      SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN }}",

        "contents": "---\nglobs: \"**/*.test.{ts,tsx}\", \"**/*.spec.{ts,tsx}\", \"tests/unit/**/*\"\nalwaysApply: false\n---\n# Unit Testing Rules\n\n## Core Principles\n\n- **Scope**: Test one unit in isolation (pure functions, small utilities, or a single module's public API). Avoid integration concerns.\n- **Location &amp; naming**: Place files under &#96;/tests/unit&#96; mirroring the &#96;src&#96; path; name them &#96;*.test.ts&#96; or &#96;*.test.tsx&#96;.\n- **Dependencies**: Never mock internal code; only mock external dependencies (APIs, DB, file system). Use MSW for HTTP.\n- **Determinism**: Eliminate flakiness. Control time, randomness, and async with fake timers (&#96;vi.useFakeTimers&#96;, &#96;vi.setSystemTime&#96;) and stubs for &#96;Math.random&#96;.\n- **Structure**: Use Arrange–Act–Assert; name tests by behavior (\"should … when …\").\n- **Assertions**: Prefer explicit assertions over snapshots; only use small, stable snapshots when necessary.\n- **Coverage**: Cover happy path, key error states, and edge cases; don't chase line coverage for its own sake.\n- **Isolation**: Reset state and mocks between tests (&#96;vi.restoreAllMocks&#96;, &#96;vi.resetModules&#96;). No cross-test data coupling.\n- **Quality gates**: Tests must pass TypeScript strict checks and ESLint; no &#96;any&#96; or untyped helpers.\n\n## Test Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\ndescribe(\"Feature\", () =&gt; {\n  describe(\"when condition\", () =&gt; {\n    it(\"should expected behavior\", async () =&gt; {\n      // Arrange\n      const input = { /* test data */ };\n\n      // Act\n      const result = await functionUnderTest(input);\n\n      // Assert\n      expect(result).toEqual(expectedOutput);\n    });\n  });\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Mocking Guidelines\n\n- **External APIs**: Mock with MSW or &#96;vi.mock()&#96; for HTTP clients\n- **Database**: Mock repository functions, not the ORM itself\n- **Time**: Use &#96;vi.useFakeTimers()&#96; and &#96;vi.setSystemTime()&#96;\n- **Randomness**: Stub &#96;Math.random()&#96; with &#96;vi.spyOn(Math, 'random').mockReturnValue(0.5)&#96;\n- **Environment**: Mock &#96;process.env&#96; values as needed\n\n## Common Patterns\n\n### Testing Pure Functions\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\ndescribe(\"formatUserData\", () =&gt; {\n  it(\"should format user name correctly\", () =&gt; {\n    ",

This difference comes from Next.js’s default behavior, not your project config.

## The Difference

**`pnpm dev` (development mode):**
- Runs `next dev`
- TypeScript errors are shown but don’t block the dev server
- You can keep working while fixing type errors incrementally
- Errors appear in the terminal and browser overlay

**`pnpm build` (production build):**
- Runs `next build`
- TypeScript errors fail the build
- Ensures production builds only succeed when type-safe

## Why This Happens

This is Next.js’s default behavior. Your `tsconfig.json` has `strict: true`, which applies to both modes. The difference is how Next.js handles errors:

- Development: lenient (warns but continues)
- Production: strict (fails on errors)

## Making Them Consistent

If you want `next dev` to also fail on TypeScript errors, you can add this to `next.config.ts`:

```typescript
const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  typescript: {
    // Fail the build on TypeScript errors (even in dev)
    ignoreBuildErrors: false,
  },
  // ... rest of config
};
```

By default, Next.js sets `ignoreBuildErrors: false` for builds, but dev mode is more permissive. This is intentional to keep development fast while ensuring production builds are type-safe.

Do you want me to make the dev mode stricter, or were you seeing a different issue?
